hostCode.behaviour: The plugin `net.etalii.adp.generic.timelineTimes` supplies `readableTime`, `compareTimes`, `dateAfter`, `today` and `writtenEnd` over the module's reading of a time, so a rule, a form check and an operation judge a time as a gesture does.
`today()` is the date of the clock in UTC, written as a date.
`writtenEnd(relation, end)` is the id the relation's end is written with, also when it names no element, the empty text when it is written empty or not at all.

A time is read at face value, offset zero: ISO 8601 dates and date-times with `T` or a space, fractional seconds and an offset or `Z`; the same with `/` or `.` between the parts; `MM/dd/yyyy`; a year and a month; dates written out in English with an optional weekday that must be the date's. A date not in the calendar, the empty text and a time of day without a date do not read.
Days from the civil date and back, and the days of a month, in the proleptic Gregorian calendar.

Across is seconds since 1970, down is 60 units per row; a time written after a gesture keeps the element's precision, a date snapped to the start of its day and a date-time to whole seconds; the nearest row rounds halves away from zero.

An element is drawn at its begin, at the epoch when its begin does not read, and its row; a gesture's point writes a begin in the element's own precision and the nearest row, a period keeping its duration, and a value that already reads as asked is not written.
A period is as wide as it lasts; a drag of its left edge writes its begin and of its right edge its end, in its precision, and stops at the other edge.
No edit, from a gesture, a form or an operation, writes an element that ends before it begins: it is refused with "An element cannot end before it begins.".

Arrange diagram packs elements onto as few rows as their extents at the canvas's first fit allow, related elements on rows close together and a moment kept off the row of a later element it is linked to; only `row` is written, in one step.
The time ruler labels round boundaries of the finest step that keeps labels 80 pixels apart, fixed durations up to a week and then months, quarters and years, in UTC.
In the dark theme the canvas takes the standard tokens' dark surface and border, and a moment's fill is limegreen.
An element is named by the id the binding read into `storedId`; a row that does not read as a whole number is row 0.
An element's computed label is renamed through its `label` attribute.
Giving a moment an end and removing a period's end are written as the change of `end` alone, the retype left out, because the binding tells a period from a moment by its `end` key.
A point on the canvas is read by an addition as the date under it, at the start of its day, and the nearest row.
